summary: We are testing whether adding swap-based local search after Branch-and-Bound (BnB) timeout improves the maximum clique score from 99.345 (iter-1 baseline) to 100. The hypothesis is that BnB times out on dense/hard instances and returns cliques that are 1-2 vertices short, and local search (1-remove/2-add swaps + greedy rebuild) can close this gap in the remaining time budget.
key_points: h-main arm: BnB with 1800ms timeout + local search using remaining ~100-200ms. Also increases greedy restarts from 500→2000. Prediction: score reaches 100 (up from 99.345).

h-control-negative arm: Iter-1 BnB-only solution (no local search) to confirm the baseline score of ~99.345 and isolate whether improvements come from local search vs. other parameter changes (more restarts, adjusted timeout).

Confirmation criteria: h-main scores ≥99.9 AND h-control-negative scores ≤99.5 → local search is the key mechanism. If h-control-negative also scores ~100, the improvement comes from increased greedy restarts, not local search. If h-main still scores ~99.3, local search swaps are insufficient and larger perturbations or different algorithms are needed.

Key risk: The 2-second time limit is tight. BnB at 1800ms leaves only ~200ms for local search — if swap neighborhoods are too large on dense graphs, local search may not explore enough. Diagnostic: check the timed_out flag and number of swap iterations completed.
Design is sound: two arms with clear ablation structure, fixed RNG seeds for reproducibility, and the scoring metric (continuous 0-100) directly measures improvement.
